event.name: 14 August 2003 Lefkada, Ionian Islands earthquake
event.tectonic_setting: Lefkada portion of Cephalonia Transform Fault Zone (CTFZ), Ionian Islands; segmented right-lateral strike-slip rupture
event.region: Lefkada–northern Cephalonia offshore region, western Greece

reference.title: Complex and Segmented Rupture Associated with the 14 August 2003 Mw 6.2 Lefkada, Ionian Islands, Earthquake
reference.journal: Bulletin of the Seismological Society of America

inversion.method: Linearized, slip-positive least-squares finite-fault waveform inversion with first-spatial-derivative smoothing. 30 P and 9 S waveforms from 33 stations (regional and teleseismic); 1 km node spacing; bandpass 0.01–0.2 Hz; 87% variance reduction. Preferred two-segment model, subevent 1 north then subevent 2 south with south rupture initiated 10 s after mainshock; rupture speed 2.4 km/s.
inversion.green_function_model: Frequency-wavenumber Green’s functions computed with IASP91 (10 km distance spacing, 2 km depth spacing), waveforms 0.01–0.2 Hz; rigidity 3.5e10 N/m2.
inversion.notes: FIGURE DIGITIZATION, NOT ORIGINAL PATCH VALUES. Figure 6b grayscale converted using the 0–36 cm printed legend; sampled onto the published 1-km nodal spacing, yielding 50x34 north and 40x32 south reconstructed cell-center estimates. Two spatially distinct planes were kept as separate fault_segments: north seg1 (subevent 1; slip patch A) and south seg2 (subevent 2; slip patch B), with a less-resolved patch C around the junction. Each panel has its own local along-strike axis increasing toward NNE; do NOT concatenate the two local axes into one 90-km fault or treat their coordinate origins as the same point. Dotted rectangular annotations, labels A/B/C, hypocenter stars and panel boundaries were masked and interpolated before sampling. The printed image is low resolution and black/white, so slip amplitudes and shapes are uncertain. The authors report maxima of approximately 34 cm (A), 32 cm (B), and 29 cm (C); figure-digitized grid maxima can differ and should not be treated as exact inversion results. The 1-km spacing refers to nodes in the original inversion; this JSON approximates a patch-centered representation and is not recovered original nodal coefficients. Zero slip includes uncolored/background image; a ~2 cm digitization noise cutoff was applied. Minor apparent features may be unstable inversion artifacts, as discussed by the authors. The paper states that the strongest subevents are ~40 km apart and ~14 sec apart, while the preferred finite-fault model initiates south-segment rupture 10 sec after mainshock origin, ~3 sec before a 2.4 km/s rupture front from the north would arrive; 14 sec should not be substituted as the preferred model onset offset. The segment relative geographic positions and surveyed fault-plane corner coordinates are not specified, so patch latitude/longitude and segment reference_point are null. Fault-plane upper-edge depth of 0 km and patch absolute depths from down-dip distance * sin(dip) are working assumptions: the plotted vertical axis is distance ALONG DIP, not true vertical depth, and depth estimates are not original patch locations. Rakes are fixed within their respective segments, matching the paper inversion; patch C overlaps junction areas in the figure and must not be spatially merged or moment-summed as coincident geography without relative fault-plane placement. Published segment moments are north 1.5e18 Nm and south 6.5e17 Nm; do not confuse their sum with a recomputed digitized-grid moment. Photographic grayscale/color reproduction, legend quantization and inpainting make local slip amplitudes unreliable below a few cm. Plot original orientation left south (SSW), right north (NNE), while JSON segment ordering is north, south.

provenance.compiled_by: Digitized Figure 6b (grayscale; two-segment reconstruction) from user-uploaded Benetatos et al. (2007) PDF and supplied figure crop; pixel masking and legend calibration
